summary: This headmotion1 acquisition shows a provenance warning for large rotation frames alongside elevated FWHM and modestly reduced SNR, but primary contrast metrics remain in acceptable range, warranting uncertain status pending visual review.
reasons: fwhm_avg=4.677, percentile=95.96 — spatial blurring is at the high extreme, consistent with motion-induced blur flagged by the large_rot_frame provenance warning.
fwhm_y=4.874, percentile=90.28 — directional blurring in the y-axis further supports motion-related spatial smoothing.
efc=0.587, percentile=75.02 — modestly elevated entropy focus criterion may reflect motion-related ghosting or blurring, consistent with the large rotation provenance warning.

snr_gm=13.45 (percentile=33.70), snr_wm=20.70 (percentile=26.91), snr_total=12.52 (percentile=32.07) — all SNR metrics are in the lower third of the reference population, suggesting mild signal degradation potentially linked to motion.

tpm_overlap_csf=0.167 (percentile=1.48), tpm_overlap_gm=0.458 (percentile=3.14), tpm_overlap_wm=0.511 (percentile=4.52) — all tissue probability map overlaps are at extreme low percentiles, which may reflect misregistration or segmentation inconsistency driven by image degradation.

cjv=0.374, percentile=15.02 and cnr=3.63, percentile=58.93 — CJV is slightly favorable and CNR is mid-range, providing weak counterevidence against severe motion artifact, but insufficient to override the blurring and SNR pattern.
recommended_followup: Perform visual inspection of the T1w volume for motion ringing, ghosting, or cortical blurring artifacts.

Review snrd_gm=120.12 (percentile=99.28) and snrd_wm=163.68 (percentile=99.47) — extremely high SNRd values may indicate a near-absent or atypical background mask; verify air mask validity given small_air_mask=false.
Verify tpm_overlap results are not driven by registration failure rather than true image quality degradation.
Cross-reference with other scans from this participant to assess whether blurring and SNR pattern is consistent with intentional motion in a headmotion paradigm.
